source_name: Riinvest Institute — informality studies ("To Pay or Not To Pay" / hidden-economy survey series)
why_relevant: Riinvest's dedicated informality studies are the only route to survey-based estimates of undeclared turnover and undeclared labour in Kosovo, and they document survey methodology (sample, weighting) — required to judge whether cash-intensity numbers are comparable year to year.

source_name: GAP Institute (Instituti GAP) — analyses and reports
why_relevant: GAP is the most prolific Kosovo policy institute on public finance, business environment and banking-sector commentary; publishes short Albanian-language analyses (analizë) that often reprocess BQK data into series the central bank does not present, and reacts fast to payment-regulation changes.

source_name: BQK / CBK — Working Papers series (Analysis and Research)
why_relevant: Central-bank staff working papers frequently preview data and indicators (payment-system usage, card penetration, financial inclusion, remittances-in-cash) months or years before they enter the routine statistical publications; they also disclose the underlying microdata definitions.

source_name: UBT Knowledge Center — Theses and Dissertations (etd)
why_relevant: Open bepress-style repository of UBT student theses, containing multiple Albanian-language works specifically on electronic payments, bank cards and the Kosovo banking system (e.g. 'Pagesat elektronike në Kosovë', 'Sistemi bankar në Kosovë', 'Roli i Bankës Qendrore'). Theses often reproduce BQK series and add small original surveys on card/e-banking usage.

source_name: University of Prishtina 'Hasan Prishtina' — Faculty of Economics (Fakulteti Ekonomik)
why_relevant: Largest economics faculty in Kosovo with bachelor/master/doctoral programmes; doctoral theses and staff papers on banking, payments and financial inclusion originate here. No consolidated public thesis repository was visible, so faculty pages + staff profiles are the discovery route.

source_name: University of Mitrovica 'Isa Boletini' — thesis publication portal (SMU)
why_relevant: Public thesis-publication portal of the Faculty of Economics in Mitrovica; delivers full-text PDFs directly. Mitrovica-based work is particularly valuable for the north-Kosovo cash/dinar question.

source_name: Academic article: 'Switching from Cash to Cashless Payments: Consumer Behavior Evidence from Kosovo' (Zeqiri et al., JLIA)
why_relevant: Original consumer survey measuring drivers of the cash-to-cashless switch in Kosovo, with an explicit instrument and sample — exactly the kind of demand-side evidence absent from official payment statistics. Authors are a traceable Kosovo academic cluster to snowball on.

source_name: Academic article: 'Determinants Affecting Consumer Acceptance and Adoption of Internet Banking in Developing Countries: the case of Kosovo' (Economic Studies / Ikonomicheski Izsledvania)
why_relevant: Kosovo-specific survey on e-banking adoption determinants; useful for adoption-barrier framing and for identifying the Kosovo academic authors who repeatedly field payment-behaviour surveys.

source_name: RePEc / IDEAS — Kosovo economics working-paper and article index
why_relevant: Aggregator that indexes Kosovo-authored economics articles and central-bank working papers in one searchable place; the most efficient standing monitor for new academic output on Kosovo payments/cash, and it surfaces author pages for snowballing.

source_name: NGO Aktiv (NVO Aktiv), North Mitrovica — research and commentary on banking/payments for the Serb community
why_relevant: The only sustained Serbian-language research actor documenting cash and payment behaviour in Serb-majority municipalities — dinar cash flows, bank-branch closures (NLB Komercijalna), and the effect of BQK's euro-only cash rule. Indispensable for cash-usage intelligence the euro-centric official statistics do not capture.

source_name: INDEP — Institute for Development Policy (Instituti për Politika Zhvillimore)
why_relevant: Kosovo think tank producing public-policy and governance analyses including digitalisation of public services and public finance; secondary but relevant for e-government payment adoption and digital-finance policy critique.

source_name: KIPRED — Kosovar Institute for Policy Research and Development
why_relevant: Long-established Kosovo policy institute; mostly governance/rule-of-law but publishes on state capture, public finance and the grey economy — indirect signal on cash-intensive and informal sectors.

source_name: ResearchGate / Academia.edu — Kosovo payments & informality author clusters
why_relevant: Kosovo academics routinely self-archive full texts here that are otherwise paywalled or absent from institutional repositories (e.g. informal-economy and cashless-payment studies). Best snowballing surface for author networks and unindexed conference papers.

source_name: RIT Kosovo (A.U.K.) — student research / RIT Scholar Works
why_relevant: English-language theses by Kosovo students are deposited in RIT's repository (e.g. 'Fighting Informal Economy: Informal Labor' by Lumbardh Zagragja), giving methodologically explicit informal-economy work on Kosovo. No separate RIT Kosovo repository was found.

source_name: BQK — Financial statistics for other (non-bank) financial institutions and remittances (monthly news releases)
why_relevant: This monthly release pairs remittance figures with the non-bank financial institution (MTO) sector — the channel through which the majority of remittances physically arrive. It is the only regular official breakdown of remittances by delivery channel (non-bank financial institutions vs commercial banks vs other), which is exactly the cash-versus-account split that drives ATM and cash demand.

source_name: BQK — Paraja në Qarkullim / Currency in Circulation (Banking Operations)
why_relevant: Kosovo uses the euro unilaterally, so there is no national issuance series; this BQK page and the cash-operations chapters of its annual reports are the only official window on euro banknote/coin supply, denomination mix, cash imports/exports and note processing in Kosovo — the core physical-cash-circulation indicator for this cell.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për operacionet me para (Regulation on cash operations, 2023)
why_relevant: Defines the rules banks must follow for cash handling, note fitness/recirculation and authorisation for cash import/export — the regulatory constraint set that shapes the cash-in-transit and cash-management market in Kosovo.

source_name: BQK — Lista e institucioneve financiare të licencuara/regjistruara (list of licensed/registered financial institutions)
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map: the periodically-updated register naming every licensed non-bank financial institution, payment institution and e-money issuer in Kosovo — i.e. the complete universe of legal money transfer operators and their local corporate vehicles. Best single snowball source for MTO agent-network research.

source_name: BQK — Rregullore për informacionet e transfereve (Regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds)
why_relevant: Sets the AML/data requirements on every cross-border transfer including MTO remittances; changes here directly alter MTO agent onboarding cost and the friction of cash pay-out, a leading indicator for channel shift from cash to account.

source_name: BQK — Studija: Troškovi plaćanja male vrednosti na Kosovu / Study on the cost of retail payments in Kosovo (Serbian-language edition)
why_relevant: A BQK cost-of-retail-payments study quantifying the social cost of cash versus electronic instruments in Kosovo — the single most directly usable evidence base for cash-usage economics, and it exists in a Serbian-language version confirming BQK's sr publication track.

source_name: BQK — Nacionalna strategija za plaćanja male vrednosti / National Retail Payments Strategy (sr edition)
why_relevant: The national payment-system development strategy states official targets for reducing cash usage and modernising retail payments, giving the policy trajectory that will reshape ATM/POS and cash-management demand.

source_name: Unioni Financiar Prishtinë (UFP) — Western Union principal agent for Kosovo / UnionNet network
source_subtype: MTO agent corporate site with location directory and tariff pages
why_relevant: UFP is described on its own site as the agent of Western Union Financial Services for Kosovo since 2000, operating the UnionNet network of 170+ locations that also handles utility bill payments. This is the largest single non-bank cash pay-out and cash-collection network in the country and a direct competitor/partner surface for POS and cash-handling business.

source_name: MoneyGram — Kosovo agent location directory
why_relevant: MoneyGram publishes a browsable directory of its Kosovo agent locations (search results indicate several hundred points, organised by city/state pages under the 'xr' country code). This yields an independent, address-level map of cash pay-out points, complementing the Western Union/UFP network.

source_name: Posta e Kosovës — Shërbimet e Pagesave / Payment Services
why_relevant: The state postal operator runs a nationwide counter network offering bill payment and cash-handling services, reaching rural areas banks do not. It is a structural competitor to bank branches and MTO agents for cash-based transactions and a candidate partner/customer for cash-management and POS solutions.

source_name: World Bank — Remittance Prices Worldwide, Germany→Kosovo corridor
why_relevant: Quarterly, provider-level pricing for the single largest remittance corridor into Kosovo (Germany ~40% of inflows), broken down by firm and by pay-out instrument (cash pickup vs account). Directly quantifies the price incentive that keeps remittances arriving as cash.

source_name: World Bank / KNOMAD — Migration and Development Briefs and bilateral remittance matrix
source_subtype: international organisation research programme / dataset archive
why_relevant: Provides internationally comparable remittance inflow estimates and a bilateral remittance matrix, letting Kosovo's BQK-reported figures be cross-checked and benchmarked against regional peers. Note KNOMAD itself ran 2013–2024, so the archive is the durable asset.

source_name: UNDP Kosovo — Kosovo Diaspora reports and Kosovo Remittance Studies
why_relevant: UNDP's Kosovo Remittance Study series (with BQK, ASK, IMF, USAID involvement) is the main survey evidence on HOW remittances arrive — notably that cash carried in person during family visits dominates over formal channels. This informal cash channel is invisible in banking statistics yet is a major driver of physical cash circulation.
